A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ForenAgent research, and all supplied pages, tables, figures and equations support reliable comparison. Neither PDF contains an appendix: both end with references, despite referring to supplementary materials. Those external materials are outside the available evidence.

before.justification: v2 reports original FABench and SIDA-Test evaluations, component ablations, qualitative examples and tool-usage measurements in Tables 1–3 and Figures 5–7.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark results, ablations, qualitative examples and tool-usage measurements reported in v2.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 retains the same interactive framework, 12 forensic tools, Cold-Start training, GRPO fine-tuning and four tool-reward components. The added related-work description does not document a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same FABench coverage of authentic, synthetic and tampered images, the same generators and COCO sources, and the same SIDA-Test evaluation. No dataset, task or test scenario is added.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same 24 baselines, including the same three tool-equipped comparators. Table 2 retains the same nine SIDA-Test baselines; no comparator is added, removed or replaced.

E3.justification: Both retain 700 test images per FABench class, the same metrics and Qwen2.5-VL-7B backbone, and the same training settings: two Cold-Start epochs, 80 GRPO iterations, eight rollouts per prompt and at most seven tool calls.

E4.justification: Table 3 retains identical training-stage, reward-component and backbone ablations. The qualitative cases and tool-usage analyses in Figures 1 and 5–7 are also unchanged; their relocation adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Both report the same point estimates and descriptive counts. Neither supplies evaluation seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–3 match, including ForenAgent's FABench accuracy/F1 of 89.5/89.4 and SIDA-Test accuracy/F1 of 83.1/82.9. The tool-frequency counts and qualitative findings also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 retain identical first-use definitions, crop and coherence indicators, and reward aggregation. No mathematical assumption, derivation, theorem or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about interactive forensic tool use, FABench, staged training and reflective reasoning. The expanded related-work framing does not change these claims' scope.

C2.justification: The explanations of baseline weaknesses, reward-component importance, backbone suitability and adaptive tool selection are unchanged. The reference to supplementary discussion of localization limitations also remains unchanged.

D1.justification: The disclosed prompt conventions, trajectory filtering, hyperparameters, hardware and training budgets remain identical. The stated code-access link is unchanged, and v3 adds no implementation or reproducibility instructions.

R1.justification: Sections 2.1–2.2 add explicit connections between prior detection and visual-agent research and ForenAgent's forensic focus, including a synthesis of the transition from fixed tools to adaptive agents. The same 65 cited works remain; bibliographic metadata updates do not introduce new literature.

P1.justification: v3 locally rewrites and expands Section 2.2, adds a transition in Section 2.1, and updates author-role notes, contact information and bibliography details. It also adds funding acknowledgments. The overall section sequence and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The same seven figures and three tables are retained. Figure 1 moves upward on page 2, Figures 5–6 move from page 13 to page 14 alongside Figure 7, and surrounding text reflows. Author identifiers and footnotes also alter the title-page layout.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves exposition by adding an explicit synthesis and forensic research-gap connection to Section 2.2's literature discussion. More complete bibliographic identifiers and publication details improve traceability. These are limited documentation gains; the methods, empirical evidence and stated limitations remain unchanged.
